quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to check your blind spot if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume other drivers will see your turn signal and respond.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself in a crash, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How can you make the shortest and safest stops?

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both brakes smoothly and gradually, without skidding either tire.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It can reduce the severity of head injuries.
It makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can reduce the severity of head injuries.
questions.explanation: A helmet greatly lowers your chance of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: Under good conditions, keep a minimum _______ following distance.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least a two-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are worse than ideal.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop than normal, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If stopping will take longer than usual, give yourself more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be safe if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body typically eliminates one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system even at this rate, and it may still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: Motorcycles don't have blind spots because they are small.
Blind spots are so small they don't matter.
Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers are all slippery. Dry pavement is safe for motorcycles.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking alcohol. Do everything you can to stop them. Take their keys if needed and arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT and state standards, fit snugly around your head, and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks does not matter for safety.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When choosing shoes for riding, you should pick:

options.text: Shoes with long laces that hang out.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or high, sturdy shoes that cover your ankles for support. Heels should be short so they don't catch. Laces must be tucked in so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and be free of defects.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the side lane as possible. The road behind and beside you is most important to see.

questions.question: What is commonly found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars form a strip in the center of each lane. In dry conditions, it is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride on this center strip.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only when carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: What does NOT need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle's tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are dangerous for motorcycles. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates all have poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits properly if you can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it. You should be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time needed to lower blood alcohol content varies. Never operate a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.
